subject: POC: Prompt dataset & evaluation plan for AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>

Cc: poc@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Prompt dataset & evaluation plan

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful run-through of Redwood's inference options. Per our discussion, we attached a small sample of the prompt set and a short extract of anonymized logs for the use cases we want to evaluate. High-level ask below: 

- We want a 2-week POC to validate quality and latency for our triage assistant workflow.
- Success criteria: >= 85% relevance on top-1 intent classification, median latency < 350ms for 512-token requests, and no PII leakage.
- We'll provide ~2k prompts & ~5k short interaction logs; see attachment: acme_prompt_samples.csv and anonymized_logs_sample.jsonl.

Can you share a proposed evaluation plan, required data formats, timeline, and who from your side will own the integration? Also please send any templates for success criteria and prompt labeling we should fill out.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Emma Liu
ML Lead, AcmeHealth
emma.liu@acmehealth.com

Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv (CSV, 2k rows), anonymized_logs_sample.jsonl (JSONL, 500 rows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt dataset & evaluation plan

Hi Emma — thanks for sending these over and for the clear success criteria. We're excited to run this POC with AcmeHealth. Next steps from our side and a proposed plan below.

Proposed Evaluation Plan (high level):
1) Ingest & sanity-check dataset (1 business day) — confirm schema, tokenization, and anonymization status.
2) Baseline run & metric collection (2-3 business days) — evaluate relevance, latency, and basic safety checks on your sample set.
3) Iteration & tuning (3-5 business days) — apply prompt engineering, batching, and quantization recommendations.
4) Final validation & handover (1 business day) — produce report and recommended configs.

Required inputs from AcmeHealth:
- Prompt CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_intent (if available), context_fields (optional).
- Logs in JSONL with request_id, timestamp, prompt_id (if mappable), response_text, and any redaction notes.
- A short doc with prioritized success criteria if you want to weight intent vs latency vs safety.

Ownership & contacts:
- Redwood POC owner: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) — overall coordination, success criteria, timeline.
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao (aditya_rao@redwood.com) — integration, test harness, metric definitions.
- Redwood Security contact (if needed): Rishi Malhotra (rishi_malhotra@redwood.com).

I've attached a short template for success criteria and a prompt labeling CSV template: poc_success_criteria.docx; acme_prompt_samples_template.csv. Please populate the template where helpful — that will speed the baseline run.

Tentative timeline: if we receive the cleaned dataset by Friday (2026-06-12), we can start ingestion Monday and complete a condensed POC by end of week (2026-06-19). Does that align with your expectations?

Also: one clarification on PII — if your logs may contain PHI/PII, please confirm the redaction approach. We will not persist raw logs outside the POC environment and can sign a limited data handling addendum if needed.

Happy to schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow if you'd prefer to walk through the templates.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: poc_success_criteria.docx, acme_prompt_samples_template.csv

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt dataset & evaluation plan

Emma — quick technical notes from the SE side: thanks for the sample, it's very helpful. A few items to make the baseline as productive as possible:

1) Prompt mapping: if you can include a stable prompt_id in both the CSV and the logs (even an internal id) that will let us compute exact relevance/latency per example.
2) Sample size: 2k prompts is fine. For latency profiling we typically sample ~500 unique requests across target token lengths (e.g., short 32-64, medium 256, long 512) to get a representative distribution.
3) Anonymization: jsonl with fields request_id, prompt_id, response_text (redacted), and masked_user_id is ideal. Please avoid including raw PHI in response_text. If you need a redaction checklist, Rishi can share our recommended approach.
4) Format: UTF-8 CSV/JSONL. If you have nested JSON fields, flatten them; otherwise a small ingestion script can be supplied.

I'll own the test harness for the baseline and will share a small runner script and evaluation notebook once we confirm the final schema. Plan to stand up the evaluation infra in Redwood's dedicated POC workspace (ephemeral) so data is isolated.

Let me know if you want me to open a temporary S3 share (or use your Drive link).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
